summary: Grant County, OR summit lookout on Strawberry Mountain: phone line 1913, sheet-steel house 1916, D-6 cabin 1921, L-4 cab 1941; removed or destroyed in 1966.

facts.design: L-4 cab (1941), replacing a D-6 cupola cabin (1921)
facts.status_note: Register says the cab was removed in 1966; firelookout.com says it was destroyed that year; no source describes what remains on the summit

staffing.status: fire-season lookouts named in newspapers and on Forest Lookouts from 1916 through 1939; no later staffing record found

events.note: Telephone line installed to the summit; a fire on upper Beech Creek was first reported from the lookout
Fire finder installed at the lookout station
Lookout house of sheet steel built September 1916 for a total cost of $663; a man kept there in fire season
House destroyed by wind the following spring
D-6 cupola lookout house constructed; the Forest Lookouts page quotes a 1940 account saying it replaced the sheet-steel house in September 1921
Lookout received a special sending and receiving radio
L-4 cab built in 1941, replacing the D-6 cupola cabin; material packed to the summit in August 1941
Register says the cab was removed in 1966; firelookout.com says it was destroyed that year
Registered July 16, 2011 as US 1093, OR 450; nominated by Ray Kresek

corrections.proposed: L-4 cab (1941), replacing a D-6 cupola cabin (1921)
corrections.why: D-6 was the 1921 cupola cabin; it was replaced by an L-4 cab in 1941, which was the lookout's last structure before its 1966 removal

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The 1916 structure is a sheet-steel house in the 1940 account and in firelookout.com, but 1916 newspapers call it a steel lookout tower. The story reports both.
The Register says the cab was removed in 1966; firelookout.com says it was destroyed in 1966. Both agree it was gone by then.

notes_for_editor: Brief's design D-6 is only the 1921-1941 cabin; the L-4 cab (1941) was the last structure, so a correction is proposed. Brief's elevation (2,755 m) and coordinates match the Register. Conflicts on the 1916 structure's form and the 1966 removal versus destruction are in the story. No source describes the site today or public access, so facts.access is omitted. The 1946 NGS note places a survey station at the center of the lookout house, which is historical only. An oregonphotos.com page says the station stood 'up to 1966 or so' (not used as a source; no image URL captured). Research used 1 WebSearch and 3 page reads (plus a grep of Wikipedia and oregonphotos).
